_link.title: I can explain how enzyme concentration affects the rate of reaction

toLevel2.question: What happens to the rate of reaction when enzyme concentration is increased?
toLevel2.correct: The rate increases because more active sites are available
toLevel2.correctExplanation: More enzyme molecules provide more active sites, allowing more substrate to be processed simultaneously.

distractors.answer: The rate decreases because the enzymes compete with each other
distractors.explanation: Enzymes do not compete; more enzymes provide more active sites and a faster rate.

distractors.answer: The rate remains the same regardless of enzyme concentration
distractors.explanation: Increasing enzyme concentration increases the number of active sites, raising the rate.

distractors.answer: The rate drops to zero because too many enzymes block the substrate
distractors.explanation: More enzymes do not block substrate; they provide more sites for substrate binding.

toLevel2.question: Why does increasing enzyme concentration increase the rate of reaction?
toLevel2.correct: More enzyme molecules mean more active sites for substrate to bind to
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Each enzyme molecule has an active site; more enzymes means more simultaneous reactions can occur.

distractors.answer: More enzymes release more heat, which speeds up the reaction rate
distractors.explanation: Enzymes do not speed reactions by releasing heat; they provide more active sites.

distractors.answer: More enzymes change the pH to make conditions more favourable for the reaction
distractors.explanation: Enzymes do not alter pH; more enzymes provide more active sites.

distractors.answer: More enzymes make the substrate molecules move faster in the solution
distractors.explanation: Enzymes do not affect substrate movement; they provide more active sites.

toLevel2.question: If substrate is in excess, what limits the rate of an enzyme-catalysed reaction?

distractors.explanation: Substrate is already in excess; enzyme concentration is the limiting factor.

distractors.answer: The temperature of the surrounding environment
distractors.explanation: At constant temperature, enzyme number is the limiting factor when substrate is in excess.

distractors.answer: The amount of water in the reaction mixture
distractors.explanation: Water is not the limiting factor; enzyme concentration limits the rate.

toLevel2.question: What is the relationship between enzyme concentration and reaction rate when substrate is in excess?

distractors.answer: The rate remains constant regardless of enzyme concentration changes

distractors.answer: The rate increases exponentially with small enzyme increases
distractors.explanation: The relationship is proportional (linear), not exponential.

distractors.answer: The rate decreases as enzyme concentration rises in excess substrate
distractors.explanation: More enzyme increases the rate; it does not decrease it.

toLevel2.question: When does increasing enzyme concentration stop increasing the reaction rate?
toLevel2.correct: When substrate becomes limiting and there is not enough for all enzymes
toLevel2.correctExplanation: If substrate runs low, some enzyme active sites will be empty, so adding more enzymes has no effect.

distractors.answer: Increasing enzyme concentration always increases the rate without any limit
distractors.explanation: If substrate becomes limiting, adding more enzyme has no further effect on the rate.

distractors.answer: Increasing enzyme concentration never increases the rate at any point
distractors.explanation: More enzyme does increase the rate as long as substrate is available.

distractors.answer: When the enzymes begin to denature each other through physical contact
distractors.explanation: Enzymes do not denature each other; the rate stops increasing when substrate is limiting.

toLevel2.question: Increasing enzyme concentration increases the number of active sites available for substrate binding.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Each enzyme molecule has an active site; more molecules means more sites where reactions can occur.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: More enzyme molecules directly means more active sites; this is a fundamental principle.

toLevel2.correctExplanation: If substrate is limiting, additional enzymes will have no substrate to act on and the rate will not increase.

distractors.explanation: Viscosity changes are negligible; the issue is substrate limitation, not solution properties.

distractors.explanation: Enzymes do not automatically reverse; the rate plateaus due to substrate limitation.

toLevel3.question: The relationship between enzyme concentration and reaction rate is linear when substrate is in excess.
